review_candidates.title: Platform Engineer (remote work)
review_candidates.description: CloudLinux builds Linux infrastructure and security products. You will join our Automation & Management Services cell, working closely with Dmitrii Petrov to solve problems across teams and services: cloud-cost data, infrastructure inventory, network policies and capacity workflows. Check out our website for more information https://cloudlinux.com/ Inside the Infrastructure Department, the Platform cell is a small team. We run the observability platform, the company's GitLab and the CI runners behind it, a few smaller engineering services, and the automation the department relies on for provisioning and configuration. We are looking for a Platform Engineer for the PaaS team to take ownership of an agreed set of platform services: keep them reliable and within agreed service levels, make changes and recovery repeatable, and reduce recurring operational work through automation and self-service. You get real freedom in how you implement things, and you own the result: you pick the approach, defend it in review, and answer for how the service behaves afterwards. Most of the job is what site reliability engineering is about: services that run well day after day, and requests from product teams handled properly. Some of it is building. The observability platform and the runner cluster were both built from scratch within the last year, and there will be more of that. Expect the work to split between platform engineering, incident response, and helping engineers in other teams use what we run. What You'll Do Run the observability platform. Keep it healthy, onboard teams, watch cost and capacity, and maintain the alerting that runs on top of it Run GitLab and the CI runner fleet. Upgrades, capacity, access, backups and restore drills Keep the rest of our services healthy, with the monitoring and runbooks a production service needs Deploy new services when they are requested. Research the options, pick a design, and stand the service up from scratch according to good practice: as code, monitored, backed up, documented Work with developers' requests. Access, onboarding, pipeline problems, new exporters and dashboards. Answer them, and turn the recurring ones into self-service Run incidents. Diagnose and mitigate impact, restore service safely, then complete the root-cause analysis and post-mortem. Deliver the prevention or detection improvements the incident calls for Ship everything as code, reviewed in merge requests. Plan and check before every change Write for engineers outside the team. Runbooks, onboarding guides, maintenance notices and status updates that people can act on Work with AI agents. Delegate collection and drafting to them, review their output as you would a colleague's merge request, and record what you learn where the team can find it Requirements Must have Senior-level experience in infrastructure, platform or site reliability engineering, including at least one production service you were responsible for keeping up. We will ask you to walk us through it in detail: what broke, how you found out, and what you changed so it would not happen again Linux systems administration and debugging on bare metal and virtual machines. Much of our infrastructure is not Kubernetes Kubernetes in production delivered through GitOps, including cluster upgrades you performed yourself Infrastructure as code as your delivery form: Ansible and Terraform or OpenTofu, changes reviewed in merge requests GitLab administration and GitLab CI in production, self-hosted or SaaS. Deep experience with another CI system is acceptable if you can show the same depth Working knowledge of the Prometheus and Grafana ecosystem: you have run it for a team, written alert rules and dashboards, and can read PromQL. Depth here is welcome, and learnable Written technical explanation for engineers outside your team: runbooks, notices, answers to requests Strong communication and interpersonal skills. This role deals with people at least as much as with servers: most work starts as a conversation with a product team, and you need to understand what they actually need, agree scope, priority and timing with them, push back politely when a request should not be done as asked, and keep everyone informed while the work is in progress. We are looking for someone other teams enjoy working with Advanced use of AI engineering assistants such as Claude and Codex: providing context, breaking down tasks, designing agent loops, and delegating plans for unattended, end-to-end execution within defined scope and permissions, with clear stop conditions. You can explain, debug and test the resulting automation, and verify generated commands, scripts and conclusions before they touch production English - upper-intermediate or higher - to ensure clear communication of progress within the teams Nice to have Alerting design: SLOs, burn-rate alerts, thresholds sized from data MicroVM isolation for CI: Kata Containers, Firecracker or gVisor S3-compatible object storage operations: Ceph RGW or similar AWS with real cost work Self-hosted Sentry, or another Kafka, ClickHouse and Redis-backed application you have kept alive under load Python or Go for exporters and small internal services You do not need to have run every system on this list. Solid fundamentals and the judgment to pick up an unfamiliar service, make it observable and hand back a runbook matter more than matching every line. What This Role Is Not Focused On Not a ticket-queue operator. Recurring requests get turned into self-service, not processed one by one forever Not a pure cloud or Kubernetes role. Bare metal and virtual machines are a large part of our infrastructure Not the DBA, the network engineer or the security engineer. Those teams run their own systems; we provide the platform they monitor them with Benefits What's in it for you? A focus on professional development Interesting and challenging projects Fully remote work with flexible working hours, which allows you to schedule your day and work from any location worldwide Paid 24 days of vacation per year, 10 days of national holidays, and unlimited sick leaves Compensation for private medical insurance Co-working and gym/sports reimbursement Budget for education The opportunity to receive a reward for the most innovative idea that the company can patent By applying for this position, you consent to the processing of your personal data as described in our Privacy Policy (https://cloudlinux.com/candidate-privacy-notice), which provides detailed information on how we maintain and handle your data.

review_candidates.description: The world’s digital experiences run on something invisible: the infrastructure and software that keep them fast, reliable, and secure. At Gcore, you’ll help design and deliver that foundation for an AI-driven world. We’re a global provider of infrastructure and software solutions for AI, cloud, network, and security, powering everything from real-time communication and streaming to enterprise AI and secure web applications. With 210+ edge locations, 50+ cloud regions, and thousands of GPUs , your work here can reach users and businesses across the globe. You’ll collaborate with leading technology partners such as Intel, NVIDIA, Dell, and Equinix , and work on platforms that power digital products used around the world. Our vision is simple: to connect the world to AI, anywhere, anytime. Want to work on technology that goes beyond a single product or industry? Join a global team of 550+ professionals building infrastructure and software that supports the entire digital ecosystem. We are currently looking for an Infrastructure Project Manager, who will independently run projects that deploy and change Gcore infrastructure - from intake through hand-over to operations and formal closure. This is not a role for learning the basics: we expect someone who already runs projects end-to-end, makes operational decisions without constant oversight, and resolves priority and resource conflicts on their own. Projects are initiated by internal product teams (CDN, Cloud, Edge AI, DDoS) or by Technical Support on behalf of external customers. At this level, the PM owns more than Jira tracking: the quality of the plan, realistic timelines, a sound budget estimate, risk management, and coordination of several parallel work streams: architects, procurement, logistics, data centre engineers, and operations teams. We expect a PM to take on a technically and organisationally complex project - a large deployment at a new site, or a multi-vendor integration, and deliver it with minimal involvement from their manager, while proactively communicating status and risks. Projects you will run: PoP build-outs and colocation - new sites, expansion of existing ones, racks and cage space in third-party data centers. Server and network hardware deployments for internal product demand and for external customers (dedicated hardware, managed connectivity). Capacity expansion, hardware refresh, and decommissioning. Connectivity and interconnection procurement - IP transit, cross-connects, dark fiber, wavelengths, leased lines, in coordination with the Peering team. Migrations and relocations of physical equipment between sites. What You'll Do: End-to-end project ownership Setting the project up in Jira ( GI master ticket), breaking it down into tasks, and building a realistic schedule that accounts for dependencies. Identifying the critical path and key risks at kick-off - not waiting for your manager to do it for you. Orchestrating linked tasks across counterpart teams' Jira projects: IDS (architecture), PRO (procurement), DCI (on-site installation), HDWR (repair and replacement). Knowing where the work physically lives, and reporting on the active linked tickets, not just the master ticket. Making operational decisions inside the project yourself. Escalating only what sits outside your authority: budget, priorities between projects, conflicts with other departments. Budget estimation and approvals Initiating cost estimation at the Initiation stage: breakdown by NRC / MRC and by component (colocation, leased lines, hardware, small parts), benchmarked against comparable past projects and reference cost tables. Driving the project through the approval chain, tracking approval turnaround, and handling objections. Reconciling budget plan versus actuals at project closure. Technical design and architecture Briefing the Infrastructure Architects team (RFS / HLD / SDD) and contributing substantively to discussions on BoM, rack layout, power, and network. Being able to tell a realistic technical plan from an unrealistic one, and to ask architects the right clarifying questions. Procurement, vendors, and contractors Briefing the Procurement team (what to buy, by when, for which project) and tracking execution. Vendor negotiations are run by Procurement. Monitoring request and PO statuses, and escalating early when timelines are at risk. Agreeing responsibility boundaries (RACI) between the project, Procurement, and the vendor where this affects the plan. Logistics and delivery to site Briefing the Logistics team (what needs to go where, and by when) and tracking execution. Shipping, customs, warehousing, and delivery to the data center are run by the Logistics team. Tracking ETAs and escalating early when delivery is at risk of slipping. On-site installation Briefing the DCIM team on equipment installation: agreeing installation windows, tracking timelines and quality of execution. Handling discrepancies found at acceptance: missing equipment, equipment routed to stock, equipment routed to repair. Hand-over to operations Running the hand-over to the Server Operations and Network Operations teams. These teams sit outside the Infrastructure Department, so the hand-over requires explicit agreements on content, quality, and timing: documentation, configurations, monitoring on-boarding. Organizing and confirming acceptance testing, formally closing the project (sign-off), and capturing lessons learned. Risk and stakeholder management Identifying risks proactively, before they become problems, and proposing options rather than only reporting the issue. Communicating regularly and substantively with stakeholders at different levels: product teams, vendors, operations teams, leadership. Managing scope changes: assessing impact on timeline and budget, getting agreement, recording it in Jira. Flow and metrics (Kanban) The team operates as a Kanban system: no sprints, with WIP limits and flow metrics. Jira statuses are the source of truth for all reporting, so status hygiene is part of the job rather than a nice-to-have: tickets move when work actually starts and finishes, not at the end of the week and not retroactively. Understanding the difference between Customer Lead Time (what the requester experiences) and System Lead Time (what the team controls), working to the target P85 for your components, and acting on your own Aging WIP before your manager has to point it out. Process improvement Contributing to better processes and templates inside IPM: RACI, readiness checklists, documentation standards, status entry and exit criteria. What We're Looking For: Minimum 2 years in project management in infrastructure, data centres, telecom, or IT operations. Readiness to run a project without step-by-step support is a hard requirement. Solid understanding of server and network hardware and how a data center works : racks, PDUs, power and cooling, basic network topology (switches, cross-connects, IP addressing) — at a level sufficient for a substantive conversation with architects and engineers, not just to recognize the terminology. Experience with Jira (or an equivalent tracker) at project-administration level: linking tasks across projects, working with workflows and fields, not only changing statuses. A high degree of personal ownership and autonomy. There is no micromanagement in this team: you keep your projects under control, surface risks yourself, and keep the team informed on substance without being asked. Ability to work with ambiguity and to run several projects in parallel. English at B2 or above - enough for correspondence and negotiation with international partners and vendors. Documentation is written in English. Strong communication skills: able to convey complex technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences. Nice to have: Experience with flow-based management (Kanban) and with Lead Time, Throughput, and WIP metrics. Experience in multi-vendor / multi-partner projects with a formal RACI. Experience with budget estimation for infrastructure projects (NRC / MRC, colocation, leased lines). Project management certification (PMP, Kanban Management Professional, or similar). Experience working in a distributed international team. Benefits: At Gcore, we want you to do your best work and enjoy the journey.
